formulations.text: A topological space X is connected if it cannot be written as the union of two disjoint nonempty open subsets.

formulations.text: A topological space X is connected precisely when its only subsets that are both open and closed are ∅ and X.

formulations.text: A topological space X is connected precisely when there is no continuous surjection from X onto the discrete two-element space.
